scenes.sub: And why every analyst asks for it
scenes.line: What is EBITDA, and why does every analyst ask for it?
Meet Rohan. He just joined a finance team, and his manager keeps saying, check the *EBITDA*.

scenes.text:
EBITDA = Net Profit
+ Interest + Tax
+ Depreciation + Amortisation
scenes.line: EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.

scenes.say: It shows how well the *core business* earns.
scenes.line: In simple words, it shows how much the *core business* earns, before financing and accounting choices.

scenes.title: Same EBITDA, different *Net Profit*
scenes.line: That is why analysts love it. Two companies with very different debt can be compared fairly.

scenes.title: But be careful
scenes.line: But remember, EBITDA is *not* cash. Always check capex, working capital and debt.

scenes.label: A typical *EV / EBITDA* multiple you will hear in deals
scenes.line: Bankers even value companies using EV to EBITDA multiples. Learn that next!
